title: UK Bank Holiday Leave Hacks 2027: 9 Days Away From £39 Flights
subtitle: Turn 2 to 4 annual leave days into 9 days off, with flights from £39 one-way
airport_names: London Gatwick, Stansted, Luton, Manchester, Birmingham
meta: Use 2027 UK bank holidays to turn 2-4 leave days into 9 days away. Seville from £39, Porto from £41, Krakow from £29. Dates, routes and real costs.

sections.heading: Easter 2027: 9 Days For 2 Days Of Leave
sections.body:
Easter 2027 falls on 28 March, so Good Friday is 26 March and Easter Monday is 29 March. Book Tuesday 30 and Wednesday 31 March plus the weekend either side, and you get Friday 26 March to Sunday 3 April. That is nine days for two days of leave.

Heads up that the Easter school holidays push prices up, so book now rather than January. Seville from £39 one-way on easyJet from Gatwick was the cheapest I tracked last spring, though the Easter weekend itself often pushes it to £70-£95. Temperatures sit in the low 20s and the orange blossom is out.

Krakow from £29 one-way on Ryanair from Stansted works if you want a cheaper long break. Return flights in the Easter week typically land at £78-£120. Pack a warm layer, because early April there can still be 8 degrees.

Fly out Thursday evening if you can. Good Friday departures are the most expensive day of the whole period, often double a Thursday fare.

sections.heading: May Bank Holidays: 9 Days For 4 Leave Days
sections.body:
The early May bank holiday is Monday 3 May 2027. Take Tuesday 4 to Friday 7 May as leave and you get Saturday 1 May to Sunday 9 May. That is nine days for four days of leave, which is the weakest ratio on this list but the best weather.

Porto from £41 one-way on Ryanair from Stansted is the one I keep recommending. Early May there is 19-22 degrees and the hotels have not yet hit summer prices. A week there costs around £380-£450 all-in including flights, a decent apartment and far too many custard tarts.

Late May is the sneakier one. The spring bank holiday is Monday 31 May, so a Saturday 29 May start to Sunday 6 June needs only four leave days for nine days off. Split from £44 one-way on Jet2 from Manchester is lovely then, with the sea around 18 degrees and the crowds still thin.

Half term lands that same week for families, so Gatwick and Luton fares jump. Fly midweek and from Manchester or Birmingham where possible, as prices often run £20-£30 lower.

sections.heading: August And The Short Bank Holiday Trick
sections.body:
The summer bank holiday is Monday 30 August 2027 in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. It is the cheapest of the lot on leave, because you can take Tuesday 31 August to Friday 3 September and get nine days for four. School term starts the first week of September, so the family crowds disappear by Wednesday.

Flying out the Saturday before the bank holiday is brutal on price, with Alicante from £58 one-way on easyJet from Luton jumping to £110 or more. Fly the Sunday or Monday morning instead, and come back the following Sunday after the schools have gone back. I have seen the return leg drop to £44 doing exactly that.

Corfu from £67 one-way on Jet2 from Birmingham is the one I would book for the heat. Late August sits at 30 degrees, but the sea is warm and the evenings are long. Budget £520-£640 for the week, as the Greek islands are not cheap in peak season.

Scotland has a different bank holiday on Monday 2 August, so check your employer's calendar before you book anything.

sections.heading: Christmas 2027 And How To Stack Leave Like A Pro
sections.body:
Christmas 2027 is the best leave deal of the year. Christmas Day falls on a Saturday, so the bank holiday is Monday 27 December and Boxing Day is Tuesday 28. Take Wednesday 29 to Friday 31 December and you get Saturday 25 December to Sunday 2 January. That is nine days for three days of leave.

Flights are the catch. Lisbon from £68 one-way on TAP Air Portugal from Heathrow is about the best I see for that week, with easyJet from Gatwick starting around £75. Do not look at 23 December or 2 January unless you enjoy paying £200.

For something properly warm, Tenerife from £89 one-way on Jet2 from Manchester gets you 21 degrees and actual sun, with returns around £210-£280 if you book by mid-September. Bag fees can add £30-£40 each way on easyJet and Ryanair, so factor that in.

The real trick is to stack your leave. Book all four of Easter, May, late May and August early, and use roughly 13 leave days for about 36 days off. Check your employer's carry-over rules and get the requests in before January, because everyone else is doing the same maths.
